doc.title: Rebecca Kilgore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Career goals and value of playing an instrument
summary: She wants to learn and keep alive the old songs, feels fortunate, and says guitar helps her learn the material from sheet music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: No. I want to be able to sing the music that I love, this old music, and I have a stack that I want to learn. This is my goal in life is to learn all this music. And it seems like every time I take something off the top and learn it, more things go on the bottom, so I’ll never run out of music that I want to learn. I keep unearthing gems from that era by listening to old records and I want to keep that music alive in some small way. That’s my goal. But as far as my career, I just want to be able to continue to do that, and I consider myself very fortunate to play with great musicians like here this weekend. I can’t hardly believe it. It’s just an incredible dream. And record, and just continue doing what I’m doing. I feel very, very fortunate. And it’s almost impossible to make a living doing what I’m doing.
Words of wisdom I suppose for aspiring jazz singers. Has it helped you significantly that you play an instrument?

Yes, I think it has. It’s helped me in my homework for sure, because I think if you can play a chordal instrument like a guitar or a piano it can help you to learn the material and understand it. I’m always leery of singers who learn songs from other singers’ recordings, just by ear. I mean I’m sure that’s a valid way to do it, but I always like to know what the correct melody was as written. And I try to get the sheet music and know, from the source, what it was like. And so I think the guitar for me is a great tool to help me learn how the music — the inner workings of the music rather than just someone else’s interpretation of it. So yeah, I would encourage any singer to play an instrument if possible.
